name: hermes-web-terminal
description: A Python-based web terminal that hosts the hermes CLI tool, providing a browser-based UI with password authentication.

userStories.title: Project Setup and Tooling Configuration
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to set up the uv project structure under src/hermeswebterminal/ with proper ruff and pyright configuration so that we have a solid foundation for development.
acceptanceCriteria: pyproject.toml configured with ruff and pyright as dependencies
ruff.toml or [tool.ruff] in pyproject.toml with strict settings
Entry point defined as console script hermes-web-terminal

userStories.title: PTY Manager Module
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to implement PTY spawning and I/O bridging to properly run hermes in a pseudo-terminal so that the TUI can receive proper terminal semantics.
acceptanceCriteria: spawn_hermes() function using pty.fork() to create PTY
Environment variables set: TERM=xterm-256color, proper TERM_PROGRAM
Async I/O bridge using asyncio to connect PTY ↔ caller
Debug logging at each I/O step (configurable log level)

userStories.title: Authentication Module
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to implement simple password-based authentication so that only authorized users can access the terminal.
acceptanceCriteria: Password loaded from HERMES_WEB_TERMINAL_PASSWORD env var
Authenticator class with verify(password) -> bool method
Env vars override config file values
Graceful error if password not set

userStories.title: WebSocket Server
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to implement the WebSocket server to handle browser connections and bridge to PTY so that users can interact with hermes from the browser.
acceptanceCriteria: WebSocket endpoint at /ws using websockets library
Auth gate: reject connection if not authenticated
Bridge: client input → WebSocket → PTY stdin
Debug logging for all WebSocket messages (toggleable)

userStories.title: HTTP Server and Static Files
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to serve the xterm.js frontend via HTTP so that users can access the terminal UI through a web browser.
acceptanceCriteria: HTTP server on same port as WebSocket
xterm.js terminal connects to /ws on load

userStories.title: Frontend Implementation
userStories.description: As a user, I want to see a browser-based terminal UI with password prompt so that I can securely access hermes from any web browser.
acceptanceCriteria: Password input form displayed before terminal (if not authenticated)
Terminal output rendered from WebSocket messages

userStories.title: CLI Entrypoint and Configuration
userStories.description: As an operator, I want to have a CLI entrypoint with argument parsing and config loading so that the server can be easily configured and started.
acceptanceCriteria: CLI using argparse for argument parsing
Start both HTTP and WebSocket servers

userStories.title: Graceful Shutdown
userStories.description: As an operator, I want proper signal handling for clean shutdown so that all processes are terminated correctly when the server stops.
acceptanceCriteria: Kill spawned PTY processes on shutdown
Exit with code 0 on clean shutdown

userStories.title: Systemd Service File
userStories.description: As an operator, I want a systemd service file for auto-start on boot so that hermes-web-terminal runs reliably in production.

userStories.title: README Documentation
userStories.description: As a developer, I want comprehensive README documentation so that users know how to install and use hermes-web-terminal.
acceptanceCriteria: Usage examples: uvx hermes-web-terminal, uv run hermes-web-terminal
